title: Connector readiness broker and customer commitment playbook
creator: Sofia Lin
description: Build a lightweight 'Connector Readiness Broker' playbook and small orchestration spec that evaluates incoming private/VPC/on-prem requests and returns a recommended commitment lane (self-serve, concierge, or escalation) plus a sequenced remediation plan for networking constraints (proxy, NAT, firewall, certs, airgap). The broker is a cross-functional decision artifact: it standardizes acceptance criteria, aligns SLA commitments, and reduces manual back-and-forth with customers.
acceptance_criteria: Decision matrix that maps probe results and customer controls to a lane (self-serve/concierge/escalation)
Templates for communication and committed maintenance windows for each lane
List of automated preflight probes and their pass/fail thresholds
SLA commitments and rollback policies documented and signed off by Legal/Support
Engineering feasibility doc and minimal API spec for the broker
steps_to_triage: 1) Intake form auto-runs preflight probes using customer-provided endpoint and manifest
2) Broker scores readiness across connectivity, dependency, and security axes
3) Broker recommends lane and presents required remediation checklist to customer
4) If customer accepts, schedule maintenance window and assign remediation owner
5) If customer declines, mark 'blocked' and route to concierge lane with suggested billable engagement

risks: Aggressive preflight probing could trigger customer IDS/IPS and result in blocked access
Some customers will not provide endpoints for probes in air-gapped scenarios — must support manual attestations
SLA commitments require clear rollback triggers to avoid uptime liability
mitigations: Default probes to conservative rates and provide explicit opt-in in intake form
Support a manual 'attestation + on-site validation' lane for fully air-gapped customers
Draft rollback policy and include a 'grace period' clause in commitment templates
